corinthians2.10.p1.b1.text: …I, Paul, who am humble when face to face with you, but bold when away.

corinthians2.10.p1.b2.text: Now by the mildness and gentleness of Christ, I appeal to you…

corinthians2.10.p1.b3.text: I beg you that when I come I may not need to be as bold as I expect…

corinthians2.10.p2.b1.text: For though we live in the flesh, we do not wage war according to the flesh.

corinthians2.10.p2.b2.text: The weapons of our warfare are not the weapons of the world. Instead, they have divine power to demolish strongholds.

corinthians2.10.p2.b3.text: …we take captive every thought to make it obedient to Christ.

corinthians2.10.p3.b1.text: …the authority the Lord gave us for building you up rather than tearing you down…

corinthians2.10.p3.b2.text: For some say, “His letters are weighty and forceful, but his physical presence is unimpressive, and his speaking is of no account.”

corinthians2.10.p3.b3.text: Such people should consider that what we are in our letters when absent, we will be in our actions when present.

corinthians2.10.p4.b1.text: We do not dare to classify or compare ourselves with some who commend themselves.

corinthians2.10.p4.b2.text: We, however, will not boast beyond our limits, but only within the field of influence that God has assigned to us—a field that reaches even to you.

corinthians2.10.p4.b3.text: …Indeed, we were the first to reach you with the gospel of Christ.

corinthians2.10.p4.b4.text: so that we can preach the gospel in the regions beyond you.

corinthians2.10.p5.b1.text: Rather, “Let him who boasts boast in the Lord.”

corinthians2.10.p5.b2.text: For it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends.
